method: 内置 imagegen，5幅新图。原始生成文件保留，复制为 -sky.png；中文规则由HTML排字。

prompts.cannon:
Use case: illustration-story. New replacement artwork for the Chinese steampunk tabletop game The Dawn Raid. WORLD CORRECTION: this is an entirely AERIAL skyship raid, not naval combat. The old giant steel freight skyship and the smaller rival skyships are flying hundreds of metres above a deep cloud deck with mountain summits far below. Every visible vessel is unmistakably airborne, with readable giant steam-driven lift rotors, braced brass engine nacelles and suspended cargo baskets, never touching anything below. Show vertical separation and a steep view into empty air. No water, waves, ocean, sea horizon, wakes, floating water boats, shore, nautical sailing ships, modern aircraft or magic. Hand-painted premium adventure book illustration, etched mechanical details, weathered brass, petroleum teal, ivory mist, muted dawn amber. Clear midtones for inkjet print, strong small-size focal silhouette. LANDSCAPE 16:9 artwork, no text, numbers, letters, labels, logo, border or card layout.
A small raider skyship holds level at the UPPER flank of the immense cargo skyship. Show the raider FULLY from an elevated three-quarter side view, both its rotor-lift machinery and the open void below its suspended cabin clearly visible. Its short deck cannon fires DOWNWARD across an opponent's approaching boarding grapples, clearing the loading gantry so its own crane can hoist two compact cargo crates. Close enough to read one heroic cannon action; tiny opposing skyship lower and farther away, the giant cargo hull as background edge. Suspended cargo, no ground or water.

Entire raider visible in side three-quarter view with spinning oversized lift rotors and tilted metal hull, so its nose-down dive is instantly clear. A high-altitude working SKYPORT built into a sheer mountain summit. View outward from a worn wooden control cabin onto cantilevered steel docking towers and aerial gantries. Small steam rotor-lift skyships hang freely beside the piers, with mountains and a deep WHITE CLOUD DECK far below their keels. A cliffside brick workshop with warm lamps and a railway running INTO THE MOUNTAIN; dry maintenance cradle cradling an airborne ship above the abyss. Cranes lift cargo between high platforms. No actual sea or water, no water dock, no buoyant floating objects. This is a modest place people are rebuilding: restrained hope and an elegy for old machines. Aerial docking and dramatic height must be obvious.

Brass aneroid altimeter with a blank or tick-mark dial, mechanical three-dimensional wind vane, dividers and small amber lamp.
